prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first I need a few facts so I can recommend the right type of lawyer and, if you want, specific local firms:

Quick questions
- When did the accident happen?
- Were you injured? If so, what injuries and are you getting medical treatment now?
- Was a police report filed? Do you have the report number?
- Who was at fault (another driver, rideshare, delivery driver, employer, government vehicle)?
- Have insurance companies contacted you or made an offer?
- Do you want to sue (go to court) if necessary, or do you prefer to settle quickly?
- Any other important facts (witnesses, video, major property damage, minors involved)?

If you prefer, I can skip the questions and pull a short list of personal-injury lawyers who handle car-accident cases in Pleasanton / Alameda County.

How to pick the right lawyer (short checklist)
- Look for a lawyer who specializes in automobile personal injury (not general practice).
- Prefer firms with significant car-accident experience and trial experience (if your case might go to court).
- Local knowledge matters — attorneys familiar with Alameda County judges, local insurers, and healthcare providers are helpful.
- Ask about past settlements/verdicts in similar cases and how often they take cases to trial.
- Fee structure: most work on contingency (commonly ~33% for pre‑suit, 33–40% if suit/filed; costs advanced by the lawyer). Confirm percentages and what “costs” are deducted.
- Communication: who will handle day-to-day contact — the partner, an associate, or a paralegal? How often will you get updates?
- Reviews and disciplinary history: check State Bar of California and client reviews on Google/Avvo/SuperLawyers.

What to bring to initial consultations
- Police report (or report number)
- Photos of vehicle damage / scene / injuries
- Medical records and bills (or names/addresses of treatment providers)
- Insurance information (yours and the other driver’s)
- Any correspondence from insurers (offers, recorded-statement requests)
- Names/contacts of witnesses
- Timeline and notes about what happened

Important legal timing and immediate steps
- Statute of limitations: in California you generally have 2 years from the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit (California Code of Civil Procedure §335.1). If the defendant is a government entity, the time is much shorter (often 6 months to present a claim). Don’t delay important deadlines.
- Seek medical care and keep records.
- Preserve evidence (photos, vehicle damage, damaged clothing).
- Avoid giving recorded statements to the other side’s insurer without your attorney’s advice.
- Don’t post details about the accident or injuries on social media.

What to ask an attorney in your first meeting
- How many car-accident cases have you handled?
- What were results in cases like mine (settlements/verdicts)?
- How would you handle my case?
- Who will actually work on my file?
- What are your fees and how are costs handled?
- How long do you expect my case will take?
- Do you think my case is likely to settle or go to trial?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific outcome or dollar amount.
- Pushy signing tactics or refusal to put terms in writing.
- Poor communication or lack of a clear fee agreement.
- No trial experience if your case might need litigation.

If you want, I can:
- Search and provide a short list (3–6) of Pleasanton / Alameda County personal-injury attorneys with good reviews and relevant experience, or
- Draft a short email/phone script you can use to contact attorneys for initial consultations.

Tell me which you’d prefer and answer any of the quick questions above if you want more tailored recommendations.
